title: Maps from a perfect complex vanish against a bounded quasi-coherent gap
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], let K be a perfect object of D(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then there exist integers a <= b such that for every L in D_QCoh(\mathcal O_X) whose cohomology sheaves H^i(L) vanish for all i in [a,b], one has Hom_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(K,L)=0.

proof.text: Equip K with quasi-coherent cohomology using lem-sc-perfect-qcoherent. Use lem-pc-perfect-rhom-tensor-comparison-dual to obtain the actual internal dual D=RHom(K,O_X), which is perfect and quasi-coherent. Transport the derived localization to each open subscheme with lem-pc-open-derived-localization-adjunction, apply lem-pc-perfect-pseudo-coherent-locally-finite-tor to D and then lem-pc-quasi-compact-finite-tor-dimension to get a common Tor interval [lo,hi], with lo<=hi.

Apply lem-pc-uniform-inverse-affine-sections-bound to the terminal morphism X -> Spec(Z) and its top affine open. This supplies a positive natural uniform higher-derived global-sections bound N on quasi-coherent modules. Identify Hom(O_X,-) with sections over the top open by the explicitly constructed additive natural isomorphism: evaluate a compatible family at the top open, and reconstruct it by restriction. Sections preserve countable products.

For any quasi-coherent derived object E whose homology vanishes from -N to 0, use its standard truncation triangle A=truncLT(-N)E -> E -> B=truncGE(-N)E. Truncation preserves quasi-coherence. A is supported in degrees <=-N-1, so lem-pc-unbounded-derived-functor-cohomological-bound gives H^0(RGamma(A))=0. B has no homology below -N by truncation, and none from -N to 0 by the gap and the homology isomorphism of the truncation projection; hence B is supported in degrees >=1. Bounded-below negative vanishing and compatibility with the unbounded derived functor give H^0(RGamma(B))=0. Exactness of the degree-zero homology sequence kills H^0(RGamma(E)). Derive the constructed sections natural isomorphism to identify this with ringedSiteZerothHypercohomology(E). This entire argument is proved in private helpers, without new holes.

Set a=-hi-N and b=-lo; a<=b by lo<=hi and N>=0. For each j in [-N,0], [j-hi,j-lo] is contained in [a,b]. Apply lem-sc-perfect-hypercohomology-gap to D and L. Unpack its K-flat representatives and use lem-pc-kflat-derived-tensor-comparison plus homologyFunctorFactors to obtain actual vanishing of H^j(D tensor L). By lem-pc-canonical-derived-tensor-qcoh this tensor has quasi-coherent cohomology, so the preceding private global-gap argument kills its zeroth hypercohomology.

Choose the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction and its compatible symmetry by lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction. For each L separately use lem-pc-perfect-rhom-tensor-comparison. Its perfect dual equals the fixed actual internal dual D, so equality identifies their tensor factors. Compose the tensor symmetry with its invertible comparison L tensor D -> RHom(K,L). Transport zeroth hypercohomology vanishing along this isomorphism. Finally lem-pur-rhom-global-sections gives the additive equivalence with Hom(K,L); its inverse is injective, so the Hom type is subsingleton.

The spectral-sequence proof needs the generic qcqs uniform higher-direct-image bound; this unit has no replacement for that cohomological-dimension tool.

Generic left-exact-functor fact: the right derived functor of Gamma(X,-) kills degree 0 on a bounded-below complex concentrated in degrees >=1 (Stacks 05TC).
